rv.q: Callow has certainly struck gold with leading man Simon Bird, who first winged to fame on the back of nerdish, gauche, brightspark Will in the teen sitcom The Inbetweeners.
But I never felt Bird's Philip was in touch with despair (as I did, say, when Simon Russell Beale played the part) – that this don's life was a full one and an empty one.
Despite that unintended farce, there are sustained moments of gentle comedy. I quite enjoyed it.
Callow's production neither solves this problem nor plumbs depths in the piece that would make this revival worthwhile.
This is one of the most misguided revivals you're likely to see on stage this year, seemingly intent on sabotaging itself at every step.
Those points aside, I can hardly praise this show highly enough.
This production fails to mount a case.
I really struggle to think of anyone who'd enjoy this revival of Christopher Hampton's desperately dated and unfunny comedy, played ineptly by woefully, inexperienced and ill equipped performers.
What should have been an intellectual firework is here a damp squib.
